#!/usr/bin/env python3
# This script reads the selected indicators from the CSV generated by task T01,
# filters the Eurostat city values sample for those indicators,
# removes duplicate city_id/year/indicator_id rows,
# and writes the result in RFC‑4180 compliant CSV to the outputs folder.

import pandas as pd

def main() -> None:
    # Paths (relative to the script location)
    selected_csv = "../outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv"
    eurostat_csv = "../inputs/eurostat/eurostat_city_values_sample.csv"
    output_csv = "../outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv"

    # Read the list of indicators that have been selected
    selected = pd.read_csv(selected_csv, dtype=str, usecols=["indicator_id"])
    indicator_ids = set(selected["indicator_id"])

    # Read the full Eurostat sample and keep only rows that have a selected indicator
    df = pd.read_csv(
        eurostat_csv,
        dtype={
            "city_id": str,
            "city_name": str,
            "year": int,
            "indicator_id": str,
            "indicator_name": str,
            "theme": str,
            "value": float,
            "unit": str,
        },
        usecols=[
            "city_id",
            "city_name",
            "year",
            "indicator_id",
            "indicator_name",
            "value",
            "unit",
        ],
    )

    # Filter to retain only selected indicators
    df = df[df["indicator_id"].isin(indicator_ids)]

    # Drop duplicate rows (city_id, year, indicator_id)
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=["city_id", "year", "indicator_id"])

    # Ensure numeric value entries only (drop rows with NaN or non‑numeric 'value')
    df = df[df["value"].notna()]

    # Output with RFC‑4180 quoting where required
    df.to_csv(
        output_csv,
        index=False,
        quoting=1,  # csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL, quoted when necessary
    )
    print(f"Written {len(df)} rows to {output_csv}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
</solution_file>
